Page 1 of 25 MS 666 – Patricia & Archie Boyd Teater Papers Repository Name: Idaho State Archives 2205 Old Penitentiary Rd Boise, ID 83712 Phone: (208) 334-2620 Email: public.archives@ishs.idaho.gov http://history.idaho.gov/idaho-state-archives Donor/Creators: Patricia (Agnes) Teater, Archie Boyd Teater Collection Number: MS 0666 Dates: 1920-1990 (inclusive) Quantity: 20.75 linear feet Languages: Collection is primarily in English; A few materials are in Arabic, Chinese, German, Japanese, Swedish, and other languages. Summary: Archie Boyd Teater was a Western-American artist who – along with his wife Patricia – created, exhibited, and sold artwork all over the world. Collection consists of correspondence, financial documents, exhibition catalogs, newspaper clippings and other material related to their art careers and personal lives. Biographical Note: Archie Boyd Teater was born in Boise in May 1901. After leaving school as a teenager, Teater worked as a miner, a logger, and other various jobs throughout the Western United States. He was known for his “nomadic” lifestyle, often living outside, sleeping in a tent or in the back of a pick-up truck. Inspired by an artist as a child, Teater began painting as a young adult. He was inspired by the world around him and became known for his impressionist style paintings. Teater married Patricia on September 27, 1941 after the two met in Jackson Hole, Wyoming. While the marriage certificate lists her name as Agnes Willson, research shows her birthname was likely Agnes Meyer. In records found during genealogical research, Patricia appears to have gone by multiple names. It is not clear why, or when, she changed her name or how many times she did so. Patricia was born in Germany in 1900. Her family immigrated to the United States in 1909. Patricia was also an artist and she graduated from the University of Chicago (as Agnes Bruder) in 1930. After their marriage, she managed the sale of Archie’s paintings

# Page 2^page=2
Page 2 of 25 and took care of nearly all matters related to the couple’s personal and professional lives. The couple split their time between Jackson Hole, WY in the summer and the Hagerman, Idaho area in the winter. They also traveled the world extensively, visiting more than 100 countries. In the early 1950s, the couple commissioned a design for an artist’s studio in Bliss, ID from architect Frank Lloyd Wright. After many setbacks in the project, the studio was finished in 1957. In the late 1970s, the Teaters also purchased a home in Carmel-by-the-Sea, California. In their later years, Archie and Patricia started a fund for handicapped children and raised money for the cause by selling Archie’s paintings. Archie died at the Mayo Clinic in 1978. Patricia died in 1981 in California. Scope/Content Description: This collection contains a variety of materials, such as newspaper and magazine clippings, financial documents, day books, and correspondence that spans from the 1930s to the 1980s. Most of the materials in the collection were likely created and kept by Patricia, who was responsible for the couple’s business matters. Patricia’s personality is distinct and apparent in correspondence, personal reminisces, essays, etc. A significant portion of the collection is correspondence between the Teaters, their many friends, business contacts, customers, and the public. The Teaters’ professional and personal lives overlapped significantly and that is evident in the materials. For example, letters between Patricia and patrons of Archie’s art are friendly and often include conversation on personal matters. At the same time, much of the more personal correspondence mentions the couple’s professional endeavors and exchanges information about purchasing Archie’s paintings. During processing, materials were sorted into the category (art sales versus personal correspondence) that seemed most appropriate for the content of the letter. Throughout the collection, notes written in pen can be found sporadically on documents. Archie Teater biographer, Lester Taylor, made these notes while working with the collection materials as research for his book. The annotations often include underlining and commentary written in the top, right-hand corner, or the margins of the page.

# Page 3^page=3
Page 3 of 25 Arrangement: The Patricia & Archie Boyd Teater papers are arranged according to an adaptation of the Archives of American Art (AAA) Processing Guidelines.1 Some series from the AAA Guidelines are not included as they were not relevant for this collection. Other series (Audio, Oversize, Medical) not part of the AAA Guidelines were added. Series I: Biographical Material Series II: Correspondence Series III: Diaries & Journals Series IV: Writings & Artwork Series V: Exhibition Files/Gallery Files Series VI: Professional Files Series VII: Financial & Legal Records Series VIII: Personal Business Records Series IX: Inventory & Sales Records - Includes correspondence related to art sales Series X: Printed Material Series XI: Audio recordings Series XII: Oversize Series XIII: Medical - RESTRICTED until 2031 In general, materials are arranged in chronological order. Correspondence within Series II is arranged alphabetically by the last name of the letter writer, then chronologically when possible. Following the AAA Processing Guidelines, correspondents with more than five pieces of mail were given their own folder. Administrative Information: Processing Information: The collection was loosely arranged by a researcher in January 1999. In 2005, a different researcher organized certain portions of the collection and the handwritten notes of that organization have been saved. The collection was completely reprocessed by Chelsee Boehm, Winter 2019 through Winter 2020. The finding aid was created Chelsee Boehm, Winter 2019 through Winter 2020. Documents with personal identifiable information (PII), primarily social security numbers, were removed from the collection and shredded. Most of the removed materials were tax forms, financial statements, and medical records. Some of these documents, including those pertaining to the Teaters income and medical histories, were retained when they provided insight into their lives and personalities. 1 Archives of American Art, Processing Guidelines: Chapter 3, Archival Arrangement at the Archives of American Art, https://www.aaa.si.edu/documentation/processing-guidelines-chapter-3-archival-arrangement-at-the-archives-of- american-art

# Page 4^page=4
Page 4 of 25 Custodial History: Materials were created and kept by Patricia and Archie Teater through the course of their personal and professional lives. Sometime after Patricia’s death in 1981, the collection was transferred to the Archie B. Teater Foundation in Boise. A representative of that foundation donated the collection to the Idaho State Historical Society in 1998. Photographs within the collection were separated from the manuscript materials (during the first arrangement and the total reprocessing in 2019-2020) and moved to photo collection P1998.26. Restriction on Access: The collection contains several folders of correspondence, receipts, and other documents related to Archie and Patricia’s medical histories. In accordance with the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA), these records are not available for research until 50 years after the Teaters’ deaths. Since the materials related to Patricia and Archie overlap, these documents will not be available until 2031. Related Materials: P1998.26, Archie Boyd Teater photograph collection, 1905-1978. MS 0071, Charles Leopold Ostner papers, [1865?]. MS 0353, Emma Edwards Green papers, 1923-1938. MS 0469, Idaho Art Association records, 1956-1980. MS 0529, Nick Villeneuve papers, 1910-1915. Midland, MI: Northwood Institute Press, 1987.
